newsitem.title: UK: BBC secures Arabic radio broadcasts in Jordan.
newsitem.headline: BBC secures Arabic radio broadcasts in Jordan.

text.p: The British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) said on Friday it has reached an agreement with Jordan Radio and Television to make radio broadcasts on a 24-hour FM frequency in Amman.
The deal means that by the end of the year two million people in greater Amman and parts of the West Bank will be able to tune in to BBC Arabic Service programmes.
Jordanian broadcasters will get journalistic and engineering training. BBC Arabic Service programmes will also be available for broadcast on Jordanian radio, the BBC said in a statement.
The British broadcaster, which is expanding its presence in the Middle East, recently increased its Arabic language broadcasts to over 17 hours daily.
The BBC Arabic Service programmes in Amman will be available on 103.1 FM.
